analysis.title: Equities Lower / Meta & SAP Earnings / France Business Confidence / BoK Holds
key_insights: Equities are lower on mixed AI earnings and Middle East tensions: S&P futures -0.95%, Nasdaq -1.66%, Russell 2000 -0.84%. Treasuries are rallying across the curve with the 10y yield down 4.8bp.

Meta's Q3 earnings beat analyst expectations and the company raised 2026 capex by $10bn to $145bn. UBS (Stephen Ju) reiterates Buy, arguing pressure on earnings growth may be easing. The debate is now whether monetisation can keep pace with AI spending.
Meta cash generation has come under pressure. Muse adoption has been strong and AI revenue is planned from 2027. A sizeable privacy judgment, which Meta plans to appeal, is an added risk.
Tesla Q3 net income fell 43% y/y to $787mn, below consensus, and the company cut capex. Lam Research guidance fell short of expectations. UBS is Buy on Meta and Lam and Neutral on Tesla.

SAP delivered a strong Q3 with cloud growth ahead of expectations and slightly better profitability. UBS (Michael Briest, Neutral) sees good year-end visibility and management more confident of the upper end of growth guidance. SAP still has work to do in Q4 to hit its full-year cash generation target.
SAP's strong current cloud business could make the planned growth acceleration next year harder to achieve.

The Middle East conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi militants in Yemen continues to escalate. The NYT reported the US and Israel have developed specific plans to attack Iran after the Nov. 3 US midterm elections.

French business confidence (INSEE) rose 1.1 points to 97.5 in October vs consensus 96. Manufacturing rose 4 to 105.3 (consensus 101) and services rose 1.5 to 99.3. Construction fell 1.4 to 94.9 and retail trade fell 2.5 to 93.2.

Bank of Korea held its key rate at 3% in a unanimous decision after back-to-back hikes in Q3 and kept its tightening bias. Governor Shin said the current account surplus will exceed the prior forecast and growth will be considerably higher. Housing loans and house prices continue to rise.

UBS brought forward its RBNZ hike call: a 25bp hike at next week's meeting is now the most likely outcome rather than a hold, after Q3 CPI came in at 0.7% q/q (consensus 0.8%) and 3.7% y/y (consensus 3.8%). Market pricing for the meeting is 90%. Terminal OCR view stays at 3.25%, reached in February 2027.

UBS rates strategist Mustafa Caylan opens a tactical long 10y gilts trade at 5.38% ahead of the UK autumn budget, target 5.20%, stop 5.50%. He expects gilts to price out most of the 15-20bp fiscal risk premium and outperform swaps by 5-7bp in the 10y.

UBS economist Anna Titareva expects energy prices to push October inflation higher in the UK (3.7% y/y, +0.2pp), Switzerland and Sweden. Eurozone headline (3.8%) and core (2.5%) are expected unchanged because of a temporary German fuel tax cut.

UBS analyst Randy Abrams says SpaceX's plan to add 10 gigawatts of compute in 2027 expands demand for Nvidia's Asia supply chain. About 33K Vera racks could be 35% of his 95K-rack Nvidia estimate. Power availability could constrain deployment and about $170bn of financing is needed.

Brazil runoff polls show Flávio Bolsonaro leading Lula 51%-49% of valid votes across 17 surveys. UBS estimates the final result could be 52%-48%. Prediction markets assign a 77% probability of a Flávio victory.

South Africa's MTBPS confirmed a strong fiscal record: public debt is seen falling from a 78.4% of GDP peak in 2025/26 to 76.6% in FY2029/30, a fiscal rule will be legislated, and net SAGB issuance stays flat around ZAR150bn for two fiscal years.
Rates sales trade idea: buy Hessen 2 3/4 01/10/34 vs sell DBR, as France-specific risk has widened. Outright yield is 3.675%, G-spread 36bp (+11bp YTD) and I-spread 19.5bp.

Asia tech sold off hard: Kospi -3.67%, Nikkei -2.56%, China H shares -3.45%, Hang Seng Tech -5.24%. Samsung Electronics fell 4% and SK Hynix 5.5% after Lam Research fell 7.4%. The market is setting a higher bar for beats around capex guidance and monetisation.
Korean EV battery names fell sharply after Tesla cut its capex forecast: LG Energy Solution -5%, LG Chem -6.8%, Samsung SDI -7.6%, SK Innovation -8.2%. Samsung E&A rose 16% on strong earnings.

The French 10y yield opened at 5.05%, up 3.6bp, and the spread to Germany widened 5.5bp as MPs rejected spending measures, which cast aside about EUR10bn of deficit reductions. Budget failure risk has risen.
GBPUSD broke the 100dma at 1.3389, entering CTA buy signal territory. The desk keeps EURGBP lower as its preferred expression, with resistance at 1.3433 (200dma) then 1.3470.
RBA November hike pricing extended to 17bp after Deputy Governor Hauser's comments. The curve is flattening modestly with M7/M8 at -15bp.
Singapore has become a gold haven for wealthy individuals: private gold holdings there rose about 16x from 2014 to over 800 metric tons last year, mostly from Europe (Bloomberg).
A Hutchins Center paper by Chris Hughes argues the Fed should keep ample reserves but adopt an elastic reserves regime with a wide range of liquidity facilities.

UBS has a Buy. Guidance fell short of analyst expectations and the shares fell 7.4% on weaker-than-expected profit despite record revenue.
Q3 net income fell 43% y/y to $787mn, below consensus, and the company cut capex.

sector_views.rationale: AI trade lacks clarity after mixed earnings. The Street wants evidence that infrastructure spending turns into returns.

earnings_insights: Meta Q3 (reported 10/21 after the close): revenue and earnings beat analyst expectations, capex plan raised by $10bn to $145bn for the year.
Tesla Q3 (reported): net income $787mn, down 43% y/y, below consensus. Capex cut.
Lam Research (reported): guidance below analyst expectations, record quarterly revenue and earnings, profit weaker than expected. Shares fell 7.4%.

SAP Q3 (reported): cloud growth ahead of expectations, profitability slightly above forecast, management more confident of the upper end of growth guidance. Q4 cash generation must improve to hit the full-year target.
Samsung E&A reported blowout earnings and rose 16% on Thursday after a 9% gain Wednesday.

tension_points.bull_case: Meta beat Q3, guided encouragingly for Q4, Muse adoption is strong and AI revenue is planned from 2027. Fast cloud payback strengthens the AI narrative.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta raised capex by $10bn to $145bn while cash generation is under pressure. The Street demands evidence that infrastructure spending produces returns, and Lam fell 7.4% despite record revenue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Monetisation failing to keep pace with spending, as Meta's AI revenue is only planned from 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Gilts should price out most of the 15-20bp fiscal risk premium priced at the start of the year.
tension_points.bear_case: Early UK elections would see gilts price more than 20bp, and inflation from geopolitical uncertainty remains the main headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Early UK elections, or the 10y gilt yield rising through the 5.50% stop.
